gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many days a fitness smartwatch lasts when you actually run with GPS for an hour every day: Garmin Venu 4 45 mm works out to about 7.7 days per charge at that duty cycle (6.2 days for the 41 mm), against 1.0 day for Apple Watch Series 12 and 0.75 day for Apple Watch SE 3, computed from the makers' own smartwatch-mode and GPS-mode ratings.
standout_why: Compared against Tech Advisor (cited; opened 2026-11-10): it gives only 'up to 12-days' for the Venu 4, '24 hours' for Series 11, 'one-day' for SE 3, no GPS-mode hours, no charge times, and no derived figure. ChatGPT's own answer repeats '10–12 days' vs 'around one day'. Android Authority and WIRED (both cited) returned 403 / were unfetchable, so I could not confirm what they state; neither is known for publishing a duty-cycle calculation. The derived number is new, uses only maker inputs, and also surfaces that the Venu 4 41 mm gets 25% fewer GPS hours than the 45 mm (15 vs 20 h), which no rival or ChatGPT card mentions.
decides: Confirms Garmin Venu 4 as the fitness pick but changes the advice inside it: a daily GPS runner should buy the 45 mm (7.7 days between charges, 20 one-hour GPS runs per charge) over the 41 mm (6.2 days, 15 runs). It also shows the Apple watches are strictly charge-every-night devices under a daily-workout cycle: Series 12 covers 10 one-hour GPS workouts per charge, SE 3 only 7, so on a run-every-day schedule Apple's 'all-day' claim is exactly one day with no slack. Samsung Galaxy Watch8 cannot be placed on this scale because Samsung publishes no GPS-mode hours.

findings.label: Days per charge with one 1-hour GPS-only workout per day (derived)
findings.source_title: Garmin Venu 4 Owner's Manual – Battery Information
findings.note: Inputs: smartwatch mode up to 12 days (288 h), GPS-only mode up to 20 h. Daily drain = 23/288 + 1/20 = 0.0799 + 0.0500 = 0.1299 of a charge; 1/0.1299 = 7.7 days. With all-systems GNSS (19 h): 1/(0.0799+0.0526) = 7.5 days; with multi-band (17 h): 7.2 days. Garmin rated maxima; manual says actual life depends on wrist HR, notifications, GPS and sensors.

findings.label: Days per charge with one 1-hour GPS-only workout per day (derived)
findings.source_title: Garmin Venu 4 Owner's Manual – Battery Information
findings.note: Inputs: smartwatch mode up to 10 days (240 h), GPS-only up to 15 h. 23/240 + 1/15 = 0.0958 + 0.0667 = 0.1625; 1/0.1625 = 6.2 days. All-systems (13 h): 5.8 days; multi-band (12 h): 5.6 days. Full Garmin table: battery saver 18 / 25 days (41 / 45 mm); all-systems with music 6 / 9 h; multi-band with music 6 / 9 h.

findings.label: One-hour GPS workouts per charge (GPS-only mode)
findings.source_title: Garmin Venu 4 Owner's Manual – Battery Information
findings.note: 20 h GPS-only ÷ 1 h = 20. 41 mm: 15. With music streaming during a GPS workout both sizes drop to 9 (45 mm) and 6 (41 mm).

findings.label: GPS hours per $100 (derived)
findings.source_title: Best Smartwatch 2026: The top wearables for Android & iPhone – Tech Advisor
findings.note: Price $549.99 as stated by Tech Advisor (not a maker store page; Garmin's US product page was not opened within the call budget). 20 h ÷ 5.4999 = 3.6 h per $100. 41 mm at the same price: 15 ÷ 5.4999 = 2.7 h per $100.

findings.label: Days per charge with a daily 1-hour workout (derived from Apple's own test cycle)
findings.note: Apple's 'up to 24 hours' (footnote 12) already includes a 60-minute workout with Bluetooth music plus 6 h sleep tracking, so 24 h = 1.0 day at this duty cycle. Cross-check with the same formula as Garmin: 23/24 + 1/10 = 1.058 drain per day = 0.95 days. Workout tracking without iPhone, HR sensor on, outdoor run: up to 10 h (footnote 13). Low Power Mode up to 38 h. 0–80% charge in about 30 min (footnote 14). Tests July–Aug 2026 on preproduction units.

findings.label: One-hour GPS workouts per charge
findings.note: Up to 10 h workout tracking ÷ 1 h = 10. Price from $399 (Apple Store buy page, read 2026-11-10, https://www.apple.com/shop/buy-watch/apple-watch): 10 ÷ 3.99 = 2.5 GPS h per $100. Weights: 42 mm aluminum GPS 32.2 g, 46 mm aluminum GPS 39.5 g.

findings.label: Days per charge with a daily 1-hour workout (derived from Apple's own test cycle)
findings.note: Apple's 'up to 18 hours' (footnote 8) includes a 60-minute workout with music, so 18 h = 0.75 day. Workout tracking without iPhone, outdoor run: up to 7 h (footnote 9) = 7 one-hour GPS workouts per charge. Low Power Mode up to 32 h. 0–80% charge in about 45 min. Price from $249 (Apple Store buy page, read 2026-11-10): 7 ÷ 2.49 = 2.8 GPS h per $100. Weights 40 mm GPS 26.3 g, 44 mm GPS 32.9 g.

findings.label: Battery inputs available (no GPS-mode rating, so no duty-cycle figure)
findings.value: 325 mAh (40 mm) / 435 mAh (44 mm); up to 30 h with always-on display
findings.note: Prices on the buy page 2026-11-10: $299.99 (40 mm), $329.99 (44 mm); product page shows 'From $299.99 before trade-in'. mAh figures come from a Samsung reply in the page's customer Q&A, not the spec table. Samsung states no GPS/exercise hours, so the daily-GPS derivation cannot be done; at 30 h AOD rating a daily charge is required regardless.

findings.label: Method for the derived figure
findings.source_title: Garmin Venu 4 Owner's Manual – Battery Information
findings.note: Assumes each hour of GPS consumes 1/GPS-hours of the battery and each other hour consumes 1/smartwatch-hours, using the maker's rated maxima; it is an upper bound, with no music, no AOD beyond what the maker's cycle assumes.
